threads.name: list_threads
threads.description: List the other AICodingTool threads, newest activity first. Set computer to "all" to include paired computers. Use when the user asks what else is going on, points at recent or related work, or describes threads by age rather than by name.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"computer":{"description":"\"this\" (the default), \"all\" paired computers and this one, or a paired computer named by its name or ID. threads.name: read_thread
threads.description: Read another thread's transcript, including threads on paired computers. Use a known ID directly, including one supplied in app context or an aicodingtool://thread/<id> link. The app resolves its computer automatically. Use list_threads first only when the target is unknown.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."},"computer":{"description":"Optional computer name or ID, or \"this\" for local threads. Omit to resolve the thread across this computer and paired computers. Defaults to 30.","type":"number","minimum":0}},"required":["threadId"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: wait_for_thread
threads.description: Wait until a thread stops working and report what it last said. Use after start_thread or message_thread when the user is waiting on that work; polling read_thread instead just burns turns. A wait that runs out says so, and calling it again keeps waiting.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."},"timeoutSeconds":{"description":"How long to wait before reporting back regardless. Defaults to 300, and cannot exceed 900.","type":"number"}},"required":["threadId"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: start_thread
threads.description: Start a new AICodingTool thread on its own prompt and run it. Use when the user asks for separate pieces of work to run side by side, one thread per piece. The new thread runs with the permission policy the app is set to on the computer it runs on, except a reviewer, which starts on Auto, or on Bypass where its engine has no Auto; write a prompt that stands on its own. It starts in this thread's checkout, worktree included. Pass worktree to give it an isolated checkout instead, which is what you want when it edits the same files as this thread.

threads.name: message_thread
threads.description: Send a message to another thread, on this computer or a paired one. A thread that is working reads it in the run already going, and an idle one starts a run on it. To learn where a thread stands, read it with read_thread instead.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."},"text":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":1000000,"description":"The message to send."}},"required":["threadId","text"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: set_thread_role
threads.description: Give a thread its part beside the others, or take it off. The role shows on the thread's row and in list_threads. A coordinator changes no files itself and delegates to threads it starts, and keeps its role until the user changes it; the other roles change nothing about what the thread may do.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."},"role":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string","enum":["coordinator","implementer","reviewer","researcher"]},{"type":"null"}],"description":"coordinator, implementer, reviewer, or researcher. null takes the role off."}},"required":["threadId","role"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: archive_thread
threads.description: Archive a thread, which also cancels a run it still has going and retires its automation. Archived threads stay recoverable for five days. This throws away work in progress, so only archive when the user asked for it.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."}},"required":["threadId"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: dismiss_thread
threads.description: Dismiss a thread, taking it out of Priority as the sidebar's Dismiss does. Use when the user asks to dismiss a thread, such as this one once its last step is done. Dismissing this thread while it runs takes effect when this turn finishes; a turn that fails still surfaces.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"description":"The thread's ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title. Omit to dismiss this thread.","type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256}},"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: move_to_worktree
threads.description: Move a thread into a new worktree, one the project already has, or back to the project checkout, as the thread menu's Move to worktree does. This is how a thread works in a worktree: use it whenever the user asks for one, never git worktree, so the app knows where the thread works. File changes already made stay in the old checkout. Moving this thread waits for this turn to end, and its next turn starts in the new checkout, on its own when you pass then. Another thread must not be running.

Omit or null to move this thread.","anyOf":[{"type":"string","maxLength":256},{"type":"null"}]},"worktreeId":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string","maxLength":256},{"type":"null"}],"description":"\"new\" for a new worktree, the ID of one list_threads reports, or null for the project checkout."},"then":{"anyOf":[{"type":"string","maxLength":1000000},{"type":"null"}],"description":"When moving this thread, whatever else the user asked for along with the move, written as instructions to yourself. This thread's next turn starts in the new checkout on its own with it. null when the move is all the user asked for, or when moving another thread."}},"required":["worktreeId","then"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}

threads.name: delete_worktree
threads.description: Delete a worktree the app made, by the id list_threads reports. Uncommitted work is committed first so it stays recoverable, then the folder is removed; git-ignored files are lost. Every thread in it moves back to the project checkout. Refused while any of those threads is running. Only delete when the user asked for it, such as cleaning up after coordinated work is done.

threads.name: stop_thread
threads.description: Stop the run a thread has going, leaving the thread itself alone. This throws away work in progress, so only stop a run when the user asked for it.
threads.inputSchema: {"type":"object","properties":{"threadId":{"type":"string","minLength":1,"maxLength":256,"description":"The thread's known ID, an unambiguous prefix of it, or its exact title, on this computer or a paired one. Use list_threads only if you need to discover the target."}},"required":["threadId"],"$schema":"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}
